title: He asked God a question…
paragraphs:
He asked God a question…
and didn’t like the answer.

Because what God said next…
shattered everything he thought he knew.

Praying.
Waiting.
Watching things fall apart anyway.
And deep down—beneath the worship songs, beneath the “I’m okay” smile—
There’s a question you’re afraid to say out loud:
“How long, Lord, must I call for help, but You do not listen?” (Habakkuk 1:2)
This wasn’t a man far from God.

A man who knew God…
and still didn’t understand Him.
And here’s where it cuts deep—
But not the way we expect.
You’d think that would comfort him.

God tells Habakkuk He’s raising up a violent nation—
a ruthless force—to judge His people.
And suddenly, Habakkuk’s problem isn’t just suffering.
This is where many people quietly walk away.
But when God’s ways feel confusing—
We don’t just want God to act.
We want Him to act our way.
We want control dressed up as faith.
But God doesn’t submit to our understanding.
“I will stand at my watch and station myself on the ramparts; I will look to see what He will say to me…” (Habakkuk 2:1)
This is the detail most people miss.
Even when he doesn’t like what he heard last time.
Not by having all the answers.
Because faith isn’t just believing God can.
It’s trusting God when you don’t understand why He did.
Now here’s where the story turns.
And it’s not what you expect.
Habakkuk doesn’t get a new situation.
“Though the fig tree does not bud and there are no grapes on the vines… yet I will rejoice in the Lord.” (Habakkuk 3:17–18)
How does a man go from questioning God…
God’s faithfulness is not measured by what I see…
And this is where your story collides with his.
Because some of you are in that exact place right now.
and God’s answer didn’t make sense.
your heart started to pull back.
Because the real issue isn’t just confusion.
The belief that God should run His universe…
in a way that makes sense to you.
That if you were in charge—
And we don’t say it out loud.
“God, I wouldn’t have done it like this.”
The same whisper from the garden:
If God were small enough for you to fully understand—
He wouldn’t be big enough to save you.
Because Habakkuk’s cry echoes into a greater moment.
“My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?” (Matthew 27:46)
Your demand to understand everything before you trust.
you’re not speaking to a distant ruler.
You’re speaking to a Savior who has already entered your confusion…
Even when you don’t understand Him.
Even when His ways feel hidden.
Even when your prayers seem unanswered.
So what do you do now?
But because Jesus already proved He’s trustworthy.
Stop measuring God by your circumstances…
and start seeing your circumstances through God.
Because the same God you’re questioning—
is the One who died to save you.
If something in you is stirring—
if you know God is calling you deeper—
Say this, even if your voice shakes:

“Lord, I don’t understand…
but I trust You.”
